name: Board Presentation
description: Slide-like scrolling narrative for a board or investor audience: charcoal ground, one vivid vermilion accent, very large type, one idea per section.
note: Initial version: dark charcoal base with a darker mode, four components.

bundle.guidance:
# Board Presentation

A narrative deck read as one scrolling document. Each section is a slide: one
idea, stated at a size nobody can misread, with the evidence directly under it.

## Principles

1. **One idea per section.** If a section needs two headings, it is two
   sections. The heading *is* the argument, not a topic label.
2. **Say the number out loud.** A board remembers a figure at display size and
   forgets the same figure inside a sentence.
3. **Dark, confident, quiet.** Charcoal ground, one vivid accent. Restraint in
   colour buys emphasis where it is spent.

## Layout grid

Full-bleed sections stacked vertically, each with `--space-xl` of vertical
padding and content capped at `56rem`, centred. No columns, no sidebars. A
section holds a heading, at most one supporting paragraph, and at most one
visual (chart, table or statement block). Never two visuals in one section.

## Typography

Headings are Archivo at `--size-h1` (section openers) and `--size-h2`
(sub-points), with `--line-tight` — these are meant to look oversized. Body is
Inter at `--size-body`, which is large by web standards on purpose; a board
member reads this on a laptop at arm's length. Never use `--size-small` for
anything but source attributions.

## Colour usage

Text is near-white on `--color-bg-page`. The vermilion accent
(`--color-brand-primary`) appears at most twice per section: the statement
number, and one chart series or one underline. Everything else is greyscale.
Never use the accent as a background for more than a badge-sized area, and
never for a status that is not urgent.

## Charts

Chart.js. One chart per section, maximum three series, axis labels only where
they carry meaning. Start the y-axis at zero unless the section explicitly
argues about a narrow band, and say so in the caption when it does not. No
legend if the series can be labelled directly.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart LR` only, three to six nodes, for a strategy or a sequence
of bets. If it needs more nodes, it belongs in an appendix, not the deck.

## Components and when to use each

- `statement` — the opening of a section: an oversized headline with one line
  of support. Every major section starts with one.
- `big-number` — a single figure at display size with a caption. Use when the
  whole section exists to land that number.
- `bullet-row` — two to four short parallel points side by side. The only
  approved way to show a list; never a long bulleted column.
- `source-note` — small print under a chart or table naming the data source
  and period.

## Do / don't

- **Do** write headings as complete claims: "Enterprise now funds the roadmap".
- **Do** keep every section readable without the one before it.
- **Don't** put more than roughly fifty words of body copy in a section.
- **Don't** use tables for narrative; use them only for backup figures.
- **Don't** add a second accent colour, ever.

components.name: statement
components.description: Oversized section opener: the claim plus one supporting line.
components.when_to_use: The first element of every major section.
components.html:
Enterprise now funds the roadmap.

Three of four new logos in Q3 were above $250k ACV.

components.name: big-number
components.description: A single figure at display size with a caption.
components.when_to_use: When the section exists to land one number.
components.html: 683% Three-year return on investment, audited

components.name: bullet-row
components.description: Two to four parallel short points, side by side.
components.when_to_use: The only approved list form. Never a long vertical column of bullets.
components.html:
Land

Two pilots per quarter.

Expand

Seat growth inside year one.

Renew

Multi-year by default.

components.name: source-note
components.description: Small print naming the data source and period.
components.when_to_use: Under every chart or table that uses numbers the board will quote.

charts.notes: One chart per section, max three series, zero-based y-axis unless the caption says otherwise.

diagrams.notes: flowchart LR, three to six nodes; anything larger goes to an appendix.
